_meta.labeler: Claude (Fable 5.1), in the coding session that built this repo, 2026-10-24
_meta.method: The 948 call summaries collapse to ~45 semantic templates once roles, teams, numbers, product modules and competitor names are normalised (<ROLE>, <TEAM>, <N>, <PCT>, <PRODUCT>, <COMPETITOR>). Each template was read and labelled once against the schema in src/prompts.py::LABELER_PROMPT. src/labeler.py expands template labels to every account; anything that matches no template falls back to the keyword tagger and is marked label_source=keyword.

schema.confidence: 0-1, the labeler's confidence that the intent label is right

templates.template: Check-in was positive but brief. <TEAM> team has embedded the tool in their workflow.
templates.rationale: Healthy, embedded, no ask.

templates.template: Mid-quarter sync. <ROLE> is happy with <TEAM> response times. No changes planned.
templates.rationale: Satisfied; explicitly no change.

templates.template: Brief call with <ROLE>. Budget is flat for next year. Happy but no plans to expand seats.
templates.rationale: Flat budget is not a cut; happy. No expansion.

templates.template: Quick check-in — everything running smoothly. <ROLE> is focused on other priorities this quarter.
templates.rationale: Stable; low attention from sponsor but no negative signal.

templates.template: Account is in maintenance mode. <ROLE> sees us as a reliable tool, not a strategic priority.
templates.rationale: Not strategic is a soft long-term risk, but no action signal; kept neutral so it does not inflate the risk list.

templates.template: No escalations this quarter. <ROLE> mentioned the team is comfortable with current functionality.
templates.rationale: Explicitly calm.

templates.template: Account is using the platform as expected. <TEAM> adoption is moderate. No new asks.
templates.rationale: As expected, no asks.

templates.template: <TEAM> tickets are low. <TEAM> team uses <TEAM> daily. Stable relationship, nothing urgent.
templates.rationale: Stable.

templates.template: Renewal conversation went smoothly. <ROLE> confirmed they plan to continue at the current level.
templates.rationale: Renewal confirmed at current level.

templates.template: Solid account. <TEAM> uses <TEAM> consistently. <ROLE> may revisit expansion in Q3.
templates.rationale: Latent expansion interest ('may revisit') but no commitment; neutral with a note for the brief.

templates.template: Friendly call. Client appreciates the stability of the platform. No risk signals detected.
templates.rationale: Explicitly no risk.

templates.template: Routine QBR completed. Account is satisfied with current usage across <TEAM>. No expansion planned.
templates.rationale: Satisfied, no expansion.

templates.template: Check-in with <ROLE>. Steady usage, no complaints. They'll re-evaluate at next renewal cycle.
templates.rationale: 'Re-evaluate at renewal' is normal procurement language, not a threat.

templates.template: Product feedback session — they'd like improvements to <PRODUCT> but overall satisfied.
templates.rationale: Feature requests from a satisfied customer.

templates.template: Annual review meeting. The account values <PRODUCT> but isn't looking to grow usage right now.
templates.rationale: Values product; explicitly not growing now.

templates.template: Account mentioned considering <PRODUCT> upgrades but not until next fiscal year.
templates.rationale: Future interest in a module, deferred beyond this quarter; neutral now, worth a talking point.

templates.template: <ROLE> asked about enterprise pricing tiers. They're planning to double their usage in <TEAM>.
templates.rationale: Pricing-tier question plus a stated plan to double usage.

templates.template: <ROLE> mentioned board-level visibility for our <TEAM>. Planning expansion into <TEAM>.
templates.rationale: Board visibility and planned expansion to a new team.

templates.template: Upsell discussion went very well. <ROLE> has internal buy-in and wants to fast-track <N> new seats.
templates.rationale: Explicit seat upsell with buy-in.

templates.template: Client running an internal case study on our impact. <ROLE> plans to use <TEAM> to expand to <TEAM>.
templates.rationale: Case study to justify expansion into another team.

templates.template: Exciting call with <ROLE>. They want to roll out to <TEAM> — requesting <N> additional seats.
templates.rationale: Concrete seat request for a new team.

templates.template: Executive sponsor <ROLE> is championing a company-wide expansion. Budget already approved for <N> new seats.
templates.rationale: Budget approved; strongest growth signal in the set.

templates.template: Multi-year deal discussion initiated by <ROLE>. They want to lock in rates for an expanded <N>-seat contract.
templates.rationale: Multi-year plus expanded seats.

templates.template: Client saw great results in <TEAM> and wants to extend to two more teams. Discussing <N> seat add-on.
templates.rationale: Two more teams, seat add-on in discussion.

templates.template: Strategic planning session with <ROLE>. They see us as core infrastructure for <TEAM> going forward.
templates.rationale: Strategic positioning without a concrete ask; growth intent, type unknown.

templates.template: Account achieved measurable ROI — <ROLE> is using this to justify expansion to <TEAM> leadership.
templates.rationale: ROI used internally to justify expansion.

templates.template: Champion <ROLE> got promoted and is now pushing adoption across all of <TEAM>. Requesting <N> seats.
templates.rationale: Promoted champion, concrete seat request.

templates.template: Strong adoption metrics led <ROLE> to propose adding <N> seats before end of quarter.
templates.rationale: Seat proposal with a deadline this quarter.

templates.template: New use case identified in <TEAM>. <ROLE> requesting scoping call for <N> additional licenses.
templates.rationale: Scoping call for additional licences.

templates.template: Cross-sell opportunity: <ROLE> wants <PRODUCT> for <TEAM>. Initial ask is <N> seats.
templates.rationale: Cross-sell of a module with an initial seat ask.

templates.template: Expansion conversation initiated by <ROLE>. They want <PRODUCT> access for the entire <TEAM> org.
templates.rationale: Module access for a whole org.

templates.template: Client is consolidating on our platform, replacing <COMPETITOR>. Expected to add <N>+ seats.
templates.rationale: We are the consolidation winner; competitor displaced; seats added.

templates.template: Key stakeholder expressed disappointment during QBR. They expected more impact in <TEAM>.
templates.rationale: Expected more impact = value not demonstrated.

templates.template: Account raised concerns about ROI. They've seen limited adoption across <TEAM> and may not renew.
templates.rationale: Explicit ROI concern and may-not-renew.

templates.template: Client mentioned they're moving to an in-house solution built by their <TEAM> team.
templates.rationale: Replacement by an in-house build.

templates.template: The <ROLE> mentioned the board is pushing for a <PCT> software spend reduction across all departments.
templates.rationale: Board-mandated spend cut; we are in scope.

templates.template: Champion <ROLE> has left the company. New leadership is reviewing all vendor contracts including ours.
templates.rationale: Champion gone, vendor review under way.

templates.template: Budget cuts discussed. The <ROLE> indicated our tool is on the list of potential cost reductions.
templates.rationale: Named on the cost-reduction list.

templates.template: Contract review meeting was cancelled twice. <ROLE> is reportedly exploring lighter-weight alternatives.
templates.rationale: Avoidance plus alternatives being explored.

templates.template: Usage has dropped significantly in <TEAM>. Client acknowledged they haven't prioritized adoption.
templates.rationale: Falling usage and admitted de-prioritisation.

templates.template: Team morale issue: <TEAM> users find the tool frustrating. Internal NPS is reportedly very low.
templates.rationale: End-user frustration, low internal NPS.

templates.template: Client expressed frustration with onboarding delays. Mentioned evaluating <COMPETITOR> as a potential replacement.
templates.rationale: Named competitor being evaluated as replacement.

templates.template: Client said they're consolidating vendors and our overlap with <COMPETITOR> makes us expendable.
templates.rationale: We lose a vendor consolidation.

templates.template: Competitor <COMPETITOR> ran a demo for their <TEAM> team last week. Decision expected before renewal.
templates.rationale: Competitor demo with a decision tied to renewal.

templates.template: <TEAM> escalation unresolved for <N> weeks. Client threatened to cancel if <PRODUCT> issues aren't fixed.
templates.rationale: Open escalation and cancellation threat.

templates.template: Client requested early termination terms. <ROLE> cited changing business priorities.
templates.rationale: Asked how to leave early.

templates.template: Account has gone mostly silent. Last meaningful engagement was a complaint about <PRODUCT> performance.
templates.rationale: Silence after a complaint.

templates.template: Account is merging with another company that uses <COMPETITOR>. Consolidation likely favors incumbent.
templates.rationale: M&A where the other side's tool is favoured.
